edition.en: Text from Chinese Wikisource, transcribed from the essay collection The Sight of My Father’s Back (背影, 1928), with one doubled character corrected; written in July 1927 at Tsinghua and first published in The Short Story Magazine (小說月報) the same year.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，录自散文集《背影》（1928），改正一处衍字；1927 年 7 月作于清华园，同年初刊于《小说月报》。

basis.en: First published in 1927; the author died in 1948. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1927 年首次发表，作者卒于 1948 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: A restless man walks alone at night round the lotus pond at Tsinghua, and for an hour the moonlight frees him from everything he must do and say. It is here for its patient, exact description of light: moonlight like flowing water, leaves that seem washed in milk, light and shadow in harmony like a tune on a violin. Notice the admission in the middle, that the cicadas and frogs have their liveliness, and he has nothing.
note.zh: 一个心里颇不宁静的人，夜里独自绕着清华园的荷塘走，一个钟头里，月光让他摆脱了白天一定要做的事、一定要说的话。收在这里，是为了它对光的耐心而准确的描写：月光如流水一般，叶子和花仿佛在牛乳中洗过，光与影有着和谐的旋律，如梵婀玲上奏着的名曲。留意中间那句坦白：热闹是它们的，我什么也没有。

excerpt.orig: 月光如流水一般，靜靜地瀉在這一片葉子和花上。
excerpt.en: The moonlight poured down like flowing water, quietly, onto the leaves and flowers.
excerpt.zh: 月光如流水一般，静静地泻在这一片叶子和花上。

gloss.en: 田田: full and round, of lotus leaves, from the Han ballad ‘South of the River’: ‘South of the river we can gather lotus; how full and round the lotus leaves.’
gloss.zh: 田田：荷叶相连、茂盛的样子。语出汉乐府《江南》：“江南可采莲，莲叶何田田。”

gloss.en: 梵婀玲: an early transliteration of ‘violin’.
gloss.zh: 梵婀玲：英语 violin（小提琴）的音译。

gloss.en: 江南: the lake and river country south of the lower Yangzi. Zhu Ziqing grew up in Yangzhou, just north of the river, and thought of the south as home.
gloss.zh: 江南：长江下游以南的水乡。朱自清在扬州长大，心里把江南当作故乡。

gloss.en: The Six Dynasties: the southern courts that ruled from Jiankang, now Nanjing, between the third and the sixth centuries; their love songs of lotus gathering survive.
gloss.zh: 六朝：三至六世纪先后建都建康（今南京）的吴、东晋、宋、齐、梁、陈六个朝代。

gloss.en: Emperor Yuan of Liang: Xiao Yi (508–555), poet, scholar and collector of one of the largest libraries of his age.
gloss.zh: 梁元帝：萧绎（508–555），南朝梁的皇帝，能诗文，藏书极多。

gloss.en: 妖 here means bewitchingly handsome, not wicked; 媛 is a beautiful woman.
gloss.zh: 妖童媛女：俊美的少年和美丽的少女。妖，艳丽，不是妖怪的意思。

gloss.en: 鷁首: the prow of a boat, which in old times was carved or painted with the yi, a water bird.
gloss.zh: 鹢首：船头。古代船头常画鹢鸟，所以称船头为鹢首。

gloss.en: 羽杯: a winged cup, the oval drinking cup with two ear-shaped handles.
gloss.zh: 羽杯：两侧有耳、形如鸟翼的酒杯，即羽觞。

gloss.en: The Song of Xizhou: an anonymous love song of the Southern Dynasties, among the most admired of its kind.
gloss.zh: 《西洲曲》：南朝乐府民歌，写一位女子的相思。

gloss.en: Lotus seeds, 蓮子, pun on 憐子, ‘I love you’, a play common in southern love songs; ‘clear as water’ speaks of a pure heart.
gloss.zh: “莲子”谐音“怜子”，即爱你；“清如水”喻感情纯洁。这是南朝民歌常用的双关。

note.en: Patient, exact descriptions of moonlight on leaves and water, with a sharp admission of inner emptiness; but the similes crowd, and the prose is sometimes more worked than seen.
note.zh: 月光、荷叶与流水写得耐心精细，“我什么也没有”一句很锐利；但比喻过密，有时雕琢多于观看。
